name: SOMALIA

flag.title: The Star & Sky
flag.note: Blue field with a white five-pointed star

lead: Somalia juts into the Indian Ocean like a number 7. It has the longest coast on mainland Africa, at 3,300 km. Camels outnumber cars. Somali poets have recited long poems around campfires for a thousand years.

facts.label: Capital
facts.sub: Largest city, on the Indian Ocean

sections.geography: A horn, a sea & desert skies
sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Somalia is the tip of the Horn of Africa. Mountains rise in the north, up to Shimbiris at 2,416 m. Most of the land is flat, hot and dry.
Two rivers, the Jubba and the Shabelle, flow down from Ethiopia. They make the only green strips of farmland in this dry land.
animals: Somalia has more camels than any other country, over 7 million. The gerenuk, a long-necked antelope, stands on its back legs to reach high leaves.
The Somali wild ass is critically endangered. It is the ancestor of the donkey. Offshore, whale sharks and sea turtles glide past the reefs.
culture: Somalis love poetry so much that people call them a 'Nation of Poets'. Verses are recited at weddings, markets and peace talks.
Every guest gets shaah, a sweet spiced tea, and canjeero, a spongy flatbread. Women wear a colourful wrap called a guntiino. Men wear a sarong called a macawis.
history: Zeila and Mogadishu were busy trading ports over a thousand years ago. Ships swapped gold, ivory and frankincense. Cave paintings at Laas Geel show decorated cattle, 5,000 to 9,000 years old.
Britain and Italy split Somalia in the 1800s. It became one independent country on 1 July 1960. Civil war began in 1991. Since the 2010s, the country has been slowly rebuilding.
wows: Somalia has the longest mainland coast in Africa, over 3,300 km.
The Laas Geel cave paintings are up to 9,000 years old.
Somalia has over 7 million camels, more than any other country.
Somali got an official written script only in 1972. Before that, poems lived in memory.
The flag's five points stand for five regions where Somali people live.
Somali songs use only five notes per octave.
The explorer Ibn Battuta visited busy Mogadishu in 1331.

myths.fact: Pirate attacks peaked around 2011 and then fell sharply. Today most people on the coast simply fish.

myths.myth: Camels store water in their humps
myths.fact: Humps hold fat for energy. A thirsty camel can gulp over 100 litres of water in minutes.
